newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alfa Q3 hit by financing, price drops.
newsitem.headline: Alfa Q3 hit by financing, price drops.

text.p: Third-quarter results for Grupo Industrial Alfa SA were affected by lower than expected financing gains and a decline in average prices for its products, analysts said Tuesday.
Third-quarter earnings per share came in at 1.38 pesos, below an average forecast of 1.61 pesos in a Reuter survey of analysts.
Integral financing gains in the third quarter were 206 million pesos, 33.5 percent lower than in the same quarter a year ago.

"The earnings report was in line with what we had estimated, but the earnings per share were distorted a little by the integral financing item and the performance of minority interests," said Suman Basal of Banorte.
"We had estimated the integral financing gain at 260 million pesos and it was only 206 million."

Carlos Ponce, director of analysis at Santander Investment, said the earnings report was good given the peso's stability during the quarter. "The report was good taking into account that Alfa is a big exporter and takes part in sectors which were not having their best moments," he said.
"It got over that with a volume increase."
Terry Sigler of Flemings Research said in a report that the increase in sales volume was not enough to compensate for an overall decrease in average prices.

"A consolidated sales volume increase of one percent was not enough to overpower an average three percent decline in overall prices," Sigler wrote, noting that petrochemical unit Alpek suffered a 10 percent average drop in prices.
Flemings reiterated its hold recommendation for Alfa "because we do not expect significant revenue or operating income growth for the next six to nine months."

"However, future capacity expansions, a venture into international long distance telecommunications and a low relative valuation should enable the shares to trade more or less in line with the Bolsa," Sigler wrote.
That would continue "until domestic demand improves, planned capacity expansions are realized and (telecomms venture) Alestra's earning potential is better understood."
Investors would likely split into two camps, one long-term which would see Alfa stock as "still inexpensive despite a less optimistic growth outlook," Sigler said.

The other camp "may believe that the risks associated with declining petrochemical prices, a strong peso and a blundering domestic economic recovery negatively impacting food and steel demand are too great in light of the less favorable outlook for Alfa's revenue and operating income growth over the next six to nine months," he said.
